Subject: MAP health check - procurement hold is pushing our close out ~3w

Hi Jonas / Marissa / Karthik,

Quick note - procurement just told us the security appendix will need legal review and vendor accreditation validation before purchase order issuance. That adds an immediate 2-3 week delay on our side unless we can provide the audit artifact they request (they referenced a specific control checklist).

- what can be decoupled from procurement (early access to sandbox, pilot data ingestion)
- a short remediation checklist we can hand to procurement to accelerate accreditation
- a contingency plan if PO timing slides 2+ weeks (what services will be available and any credit/fallthrough?)

Appreciate a prioritized, actionable sheet we can use in the procurement call at 4pm PT.

Thanks,

Hi Lydia - thanks for the heads up and call earlier. We've sketched a rapid reprofile and a contingency sprint that should keep your acceptance window on track. High level:

1) Procurement gate mitigation (deliverables to unblock PO):
   - Provide a control-matrix export (SOC scoping + encryption-at-rest attest) - we can assemble this by EOD tomorrow.
   - Temporary evidence bundle (logs + config screenshots) for accreditation team - target: 48h.
   - Legal: proposed one-page appendix with carve-outs for pilot data retention - draft attached.

2) Contingency sprint (if PO delays >7 business days):
   - Early pilot (non-production sandbox) provisioned under MSA with limited token cap and explicit security SOP; expected timeline: 3 business days to stand up.
   - Acceptance criteria split: pilot-level success (data ingestion + latency SLAs) by week 1; full-prod cutover gating on PO finish.
   - Billing fallback: deferred invoicing until PO issued; we can accept electronic acceptance and invoice on issuance date.

Action items for this thread (owner / target):
- Jonas: control-matrix export & evidence bundle (Nov 11, 17:00 PT) [Attachment: acme-map-v2.xlsx]
- Marissa: draft one-page procurement appendix / legal talking points (Nov 11, 12:00 PT)
- Lydia: confirm which accreditation checklist procurement needs (today, availability 4pm PT)

If procurement pushes beyond 14 business days, we'll engage our Escalation Charter (exec credit review + interim surge to keep trial running). I'll include an explicit contingency ledger and risk scoring in the MAP.

I attached a working MAP (acme-map-v2.xlsx) with lanes for procurement, legal, and engineering deliverables. Please review before your 4pm call and call out any missing owners.

-Jonas

Lydia / team - following up after the procurement call. Procurement confirmed they need the vendor accreditation checklist ID #AC-2026-S2 and a legal stamp for the security appendix. They estimated 10 business days for the accreditation queue unless we provide the temporary evidence bundle and the one-page appendix that Marissa will present.

Given that risk profile, I'm formally escalating this to our Escalation Charter. If the PO does not arrive by Nov 24, Redwood will: 
- Open an executive remediation path (credit review + partial billing deferral),
- Stand up the sandbox pilot as a bridge (limited token cap, 30-day window), and
- Assign a named escalation owner to the procurement queue (Karthik) to interface daily with Acme procurement.

Please confirm acceptance of the contingency plan and whether Acme procurement will accept the temporary evidence bundle and one-page appendix by end of day so we can proceed. I'm also adding the HubSpot deal link (below) to ensure cross-team alignment.
